reviewer: Captain (implementation finding; not a counsel approval)
questions: What artifact is each of the four bodiless section kinds actually supposed to be — instrument class, preparer, recipient, filed or not — and does any of them warrant drafting court-document prose?
The specification declares five required facts while its documents consume sixteen values. What is the authoritative acquisition and ownership treatment of each?

finding1_noProseNeedsWriting.answer: None of the four needs prose written for it. The approved text for all eight components already exists, in full, and was rendered and owner-adopted.
evidence: The build script composes complete, branch-aware, source-grounded text for every component, including all four whose specification sections carry a heading and nothing else.

Its output was rendered to canonical.pdf (sha256 533cf8ec8ac3447f89374639d0d8fbf33b5c453c1248bf33b263da56d99b88a7) and boundary.pdf (sha256 d8ca462e258723fed6ecc268ec332a2d4bcc1d4c5f2c83cc025f7bcd8a35e1ca) under data/rcap-all50/overlays/census-v1/nv/nv-seal-probation-family-set--custom-pleading/fixtures/.
The specification's own specificationNote pins the route to that eight-component family at those two hashes.
finding1_noProseNeedsWriting.consequence: The bodiless sections are a DERIVATION defect: the section bodies were dropped when the specification was generated from the approved family. The remedy is to carry the adopted text across faithfully, not to draft anything. Drafting would also have been forbidden — the composer's first rule is that it has no legal statements of its own — and it would have produced unreviewed prose competing with approved prose.

finding2_componentClassification.method: Each component read through the §4.2 document contract already recorded on it, then checked against the approved text and against what a removal would lose.

components.verdict: participant guidance, and correctly so. It is NOT in the court-facing document set and never was.
components.removeFromCourtFacingSet: nothing to remove — the contract already places it outside it
components.why: Its approved text tells the participant which of the three chapter 176A programme sections applies and, decisively, that if the case never ran through one of the three programmes this packet is not their route. That is participant guidance with real content, addressed to the participant, and it is part of an owner-adopted eight-component family. Deleting it would remove approved participant guidance and break the adopted fixture binding.

components.verdict: participant guidance. Its DECISION is now product logic; its EXPLANATION is not.
components.why: The branch decision itself moved into the product on 27eec639c: two screening questions and one resolver settle it before Checkout, so the packet no longer depends on the participant working the branch out from a page. But the approved page also carries the subsection 3 bar in terms ("BARRED ON BOTH BRANCHES") and the instruction not to file the petition on the automatic branch. Those are participant guidance the product still owes, and they are not duplicated by asking two questions.

components.verdict: participant guidance about a DIFFERENT route.
components.why: Its own approved text says the answer does not change the mechanism on this track. What it does is warn that NRS 179.2445(2) removes the rebuttable presumption on any later NRS 179.245 petition after a dishonourable discharge. That warning is genuinely useful to this participant and is also carried by the specification's hearingAndObjectionStops[5], which an implemented section kind already renders in three other components. It is the weakest of the three as a standalone page, and if the family is ever reopened it is the one to question first — but that is a family-composition question for the owner, not an agent edit.

components.verdict: a real court-facing participant filing, permitted rather than compelled. Authority question flagged, not resolved here.
components.why: The sections prescribe no verification and no notarization, and the memo says so twice. So the statute does not COMPEL a declaration. But the legal design established one in four places — the component note ("the ordinary support for facts not appearing of record"), rules.participantSignature ("the petitioner signs the petition and the declaration personally"), manualCompletionItems, and fieldOwnership.participantAtSigningFields — and its contract is coherent with the statute: executionType is `signature`, not `sworn_notarised`, exactly matching "no verification prescribed".
components.authorityStatus: custom_document_permitted, not source-required. Counsel review of whether a permitted-practice declaration belongs in a filing-grade packet remains required, and is recorded as such rather than decided by an agent.

finding2_componentClassification.whyNothingWasRemoved: Two independent reasons. First, the classification the instruction was conditioned on does not hold: none of the first three is in the court-facing set, so there is nothing to remove from it — the §4.2 contract had already classified them correctly, which is what the contract was built for. Second, the eight-component family is pinned by owner-adopted fixture hashes; changing its composition is an approval-path act, not an agent edit. No invented owner approval.

finding3_fieldReconciliation.answer: Five required facts is correct and sixteen consumed values is correct. They are not in tension: eleven of the sixteen are participant-completable blanks the approved document prints as lines on the page.
finding3_fieldReconciliation.authority: The owner-adopted field map in scripts/build-census-v1-nv_seal_probation_family-set.mjs classifies every value by construction — `write` (the platform generates it), `rbf` (REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING: the participant writes it before filing), `protectedBlank` (SIGNATURE: never prefilled), `courtBlank` (COURT_OWNED). The reconciliation below is that classification, not a new one.

participant_completes_before_filing.treatment: NEW bucket fieldOwnership.participantCompletesBeforeFilingFields. Not facts, not questions, not prefilled: the document prints a labelled blank line and the participant writes the value from their own court paperwork at the moment of filing.
participant_completes_before_filing.whyNotQuestions: The approved design made them blanks deliberately. A court name, a docket number or the exact wording of a charge typed into a screening form weeks earlier is likelier to be wrong than blank, and the approved rendering prints a line for each. Promoting them to questions would create eleven unnecessary participant questions AND contradict the adopted artifact.
participant_completes_before_filing.whyNotExternalDocuments: None of them asks the participant to hold, upload, scan or produce a record. Each asks for a FACT the participant reads off paperwork they already have, which is the controlling rule's own distinction.

participant_at_signing.treatment: Already declared in fieldOwnership.participantAtSigningFields. Not consumed as section fields, so never demanded.

route_eligibility_and_branch.treatment: requiredFacts and route-safety gate facts. They decide whether a packet exists and whether it may be sold, so they resolve before Checkout. They are written into no document; the petition's fixed paragraph 5 asserts the subsection 3 fact, which is why it must be established rather than assumed.

finding3_fieldReconciliation.invariant: Every value the documents consume is either a required fact or a declared blank; none is both; no declared blank is also a screening question. Asserted by scripts/verify-nevada-176a-branch.mjs and mutation-proven.
finding3_fieldReconciliation.zeroUnnecessaryQuestions: Three participant questions were added across this whole Nevada correction — the two branch facts and the subsection 3 bar — and every one of them decides whether the participant should file or pay anything. Eleven values that a naive reading would have turned into questions were classified as blanks instead.

changesMade: fieldOwnership.participantCompletesBeforeFilingFields added to the packet-specification contract and populated for this route with exactly the eleven REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING ids from the owner-adopted field map.
The composer no longer demands a declared blank as a fact, and emits it as a labelled blank item rather than filling it.
The renderer draws a line for a blank item, the same way it draws a signature line, instead of printing a label with nothing after it.
The subsection 3 bar added as a route-safety fact and gate (see the companion record for this date).

The four bodiless section kinds and the petition's and order's lost prose were transcribed from the owner-adopted build script into the specification, verbatim in substance. The composer now implements the route_detection, route_branch_screen, discharge_type_screen and declaration section kinds, and renders a section's declared fields as labelled blanks after its numbered assertions.

An explicit caption contract ("captionContract") was added for a filing whose caption is not the generic two-party one and whose caption values are participant-completable blanks. Nevada declares one for the petition and the proposed order: an in-the-matter-of caption, a court line and a case-number line each drawn as a rule with its instruction beneath, never an empty value and never a placeholder token.

referral_instructions was deliberately left alone: its filing_destination section kind renders from the top-level specification block and ignores section bodies, so it already composed, and adding text to it would have been an unreviewed change to a component that already ships.
stillOutstanding: The Grade-A renderer requires a caption on every pleading document and the adopted Nevada declaration page has none. See finding5. Nationwide condition, 21 other documents across 9 routes.
Counsel review of whether a permitted-practice declaration belongs in a filing-grade packet, of the three question wordings, and of the branch and bar readings.
remainingReview: The route composes nothing and sells nothing today. Nothing here grants fulfillment or commercial authority, and the owner-adopted family composition is unchanged.

finding4_declarationRequirementState.question: Did the 2026-09-02 owner adoption establish the declaration's inclusion and requirement state, or only its wording?
finding4_declarationRequirementState.method: Read the adoption record once, in full. No new legal research.

whatTheAdoptionSays.nvFamilyQualification: nv_seal_probation_family-set sits under the general qualification of the three: "ADOPTED for the limited family-level legal-design purpose stated in this workbook. No runtime, technical, visual, payment, sponsorship or production authority is granted. Any substantive legal change or shipping-artifact digest change requires re-review."
whatTheAdoptionSays.withholdingDetail: The record carries eight answers, each withholding something from named families. nv_seal_probation_family-set is named in none of them. The only NV family named anywhere is composed-treatment:obligation:runtime-only:NV:trafficking-victim-vacatur-and-sealing-under-nrs-179-247, under Q2, which is a different route.
whatTheAdoptionSays.q7IsOnPoint: Q7 asked what happens when a component the family's own record names as required is deliberately not rendered. The owner ruled: "THE REQUIRED COMPONENT MUST BE BUILT. The reduced packet is not approved while a component the family's own record declares required is absent. The alternative is a new legal-design decision expressly removing or changing that requirement."

finding4_declarationRequirementState.determination: The requirement state IS established, and it is not "required". Q7 settles that a component's requirement state comes from the family's own record and that changing it takes a new legal-design decision. This family's own record — NV.memo tracks[nv_seal_probation_family].components[declaration_and_verification] — declares it "conditional", "Accompanies the subsection 2 petition." The owner-adopted build script carries the identical condition in COMPONENT_CONDITIONS, and the specification encodes the identical rule as requirement "conditional" with includeWhen "subsection_2_petition_branch". All three agree.
finding4_declarationRequirementState.whatWasEncoded: Exactly that rule, which was already encoded and is now locked by control: conditional on the subsection 2 branch. The composer includes the declaration only when that branch is established, and refuses when it is not. Nothing was made universally required.
finding4_declarationRequirementState.correctionToTheEarlierFlag: The earlier report said the declaration was “permitted rather than compelled; flagged as a counsel question”, which conflated two different things. That the sections prescribe no verification is a statement about AUTHORITY, and the contract already expresses it faithfully — formApplicability "custom_document_permitted" rather than "official_form_required", and executionType "signature" rather than "sworn_notarised". It is not a statement that the requirement state is unresolved. The requirement state was never unresolved; it is conditional, and it is now asserted as such.
finding4_declarationRequirementState.whatRemainsACounselQuestion: Whether a permitted-practice declaration belongs in a filing-grade packet at all. That is covered by the standing counsel review on this route and is not a separate unresolved requirement state.

finding5_renderContractDisagreement.finding: Nevada now composes on both branches — eight documents on the petition branch, four on the automatic branch — and does not yet RENDER, for a reason that is nationwide rather than Nevada's.
finding5_renderContractDisagreement.detail: The Grade-A renderer requires every document whose presentation is  to carry a pleading caption ("Pleading document X has no pleading caption"). The owner-adopted Nevada declaration page carries none: it opens "This declaration accompanies the subsection 2 petition" and is a supporting page filed with a captioned petition.
finding5_renderContractDisagreement.scope: 21 other pleading documents across 9 routes declare no caption section either, including three of the six commercially eligible routes (MS 9-11-15-3, WY 7-13-1502, DC 16-803). Those routes do not compose through this path at all — WY refuses on the "approved_shipping_component" section kind — so the generic compose-and-render path is not the delivery path for the proven routes, and this disagreement has simply never been exercised.
finding5_renderContractDisagreement.whatWasNotDone: No caption was invented for the declaration, and the declaration was not downgraded to "guidance" presentation to get past the check. Either would have been unreviewed court-document content or a false classification of a court-facing filing.
resolutionOptions: Confirm from the adopted artifact that the declaration is a supporting filing rather than a captioned pleading, and give the Grade-A renderer that treatment.
Obtain a caption decision for the declaration through the legal-design path.
finding5_renderContractDisagreement.failClosed: Until then the render refuses, which is the honest state and is visible. Composition succeeding and rendering refusing is strictly more informative than the previous state, where composition refused first and nothing downstream was ever exercised.
